audit.whatIsWrong: Neeko was called 'he/his' across tldr, tradeGood, tradeBad, ahead, loading, breakdown.wave, dosFull[0].t, dontsFull[0].t, dontsFull[1].t and the report[] mirrors, and the lane's difficulty was framed around 'sidestep the root behind minions', which is not how Tangle-Barbs works.
audit.why: champ-gender.js lists neeko as female. Tangle-Barbs 'damages and roots everything it passes through' — minions do not stop it, and if it kills one it becomes larger, faster and roots for longer. Hiding behind the wave makes the root better, not worse.
audit.corrected: Difficulty now reads off the real threat: a 1000-range root that ignores the wave and must be sidestepped laterally, on 12/11.5/11/10.5/10, feeding a 600-range Pop Blossom.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike was written as 'her ultimate roots everyone hit' / 'Between Worlds dodges her ultimate root' (whys[4], spikes[1].text, wants.foe[2]).
audit.why: Pop Blossom is 120/105/90 on a 600 range: 'Neeko leaps into the air, knocking up all nearby enemies. Upon landing, nearby enemies are damaged and stunned.' It is a knockup into a stun, not a root — and 'The preparation is hidden if Neeko is disguised', which is the actual reason her 6 is dangerous.
audit.corrected: Her 6 is a short-range knockup-into-stun whose wind-up disappears while she is disguised; the counterplay is spacing outside 600 and not facechecking, not dodging a root.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two abilities were swapped throughout: content early said 'Neeko's Q root', wants.foe[0] said 'Land Q Blooming Burst to set up an all-in', and wants.you[1] said 'Dodge Blooming Burst with Between Worlds'. Aurora's Q was again called a 'gap-close'. And spikes[0].text used a fabricated Aurora ability name, 'Q Twin Drift'.
audit.why: Blooming Burst (Q) is an 800-range seed that blooms a second time on champions — no CC. The root is Tangle-Barbs (E) at 1000 range. Aurora's Q is a 900-range missile with a recast and no dash flag; the dash is W at 700 range. 'Twin Drift' matches nothing in the kit file — same class of error as 'Ares of Blaze' for Brand.
audit.corrected: Q and E separated everywhere; Aurora's dash correctly attributed to W; the fabricated name removed and replaced with the slot letter and its real 900 range. Also written in: her disguise breaks when she casts a damaging spell or takes damage equal to the copy's health, which is why her ambush ends the moment the fight starts.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit at all — defect-catalogue item 3 — and repeated the minion-block error.
audit.why: It is the field that carries real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Tangle-Barbs 12s at rank 1 / 10s at rank 5 at 1000 range, Pop Blossom 120s, your W 22s, your R 140s.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d was a line about Neeko spending her root pasted under the title 'Fight inside your R zone post-6', and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string pasted under 'Burn the stealth on tempo'.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to answer their own titles.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 'worst wave' line gave a pronoun error and a generic reason.
audit.why: The real reason a frozen wave near her tower is fatal is that the root reaches 1000 units and the wave does not stop it.
audit.corrected: Reason supplied, pronoun fixed, in both breakdown.wave and report[4].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: LEVEL CHART DISAGREEMENT, LEFT ALONE DELIBERATELY. phases[0..6].side all read 'Skill' while content win[0..6] all read 'Aurora' — seven rows rendering two different answers.
audit.why: Unlike the other matchups in this slice I cannot resolve it from the data. packet.levelChart says Aurora x7, but the win rate is 48.16% over 517 games — Aurora is losing this matchup slightly, so 'Aurora wins every stage' is not supportable, and 'Skill' across the board contradicts the packet chart. The kit does not settle it either: Neeko out-ranges Aurora at every level (E 1000, W 900, Q 800 against Aurora's Q 900 / E 825).
audit.corrected: No side, rating or win[] edit proposed. Recorded in questionsForUser instead — a stale row is a smaller problem than a row that argues with itself, and guessing here would move a chart on a matchup Aurora actually loses.

audit.why: 48.16% over 517 games; no edit. Note this is the one matchup in my slice where Aurora is under 50%, and diff EVEN / 5.5.10 is a fair reading of it.

notes: CHART LEFT ALONE ON PURPOSE: phases[0..6].side all read 'Skill' while content win[0..6] all read 'Aurora' — a live seven-row disagreement, but this is the one matchup in my slice where I could not resolve it. packet.levelChart says Aurora x7, yet the win rate is 48.16% over 517 games, so 'Aurora wins every stage' is not defensible, and flipping win[] to 'Skill' would contradict the packet chart. Per the chart rule I changed no side, no rating and no win[] row. It needs a human call — see questionsForUser. TWO ABILITIES WERE SWAPPED THROUGHOUT: content early called Blooming Burst 'Neeko's Q root' and wants.foe[0] said the Q sets up the all-in. Blooming Burst (Q) is an 800-range seed with no CC; the root is Tangle-Barbs (E) at 1000 range. MINION-BLOCK ERROR, FIXED IN FOUR PLACES: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t and the winCon all told the reader to sidestep the root 'behind minions'. Riot's text is 'damages and roots everything it passes through', and it becomes larger, faster and longer-rooting if it kills a unit — standing behind the wave makes it worse. The correct instruction is lateral. ULT MISDESCRIBED: whys[4], spikes[1].text and wants.foe[2] called Pop Blossom a root. It is a knockup on the leap and a stun on landing, 600 range, and its wind-up is hidden while she is disguised. FABRICATION KILLED: spikes[0].text used 'Q Twin Drift' for Aurora's Q — no such name in the kit file. Not replaced with a guess; the slot letter and the real 900 range were used instead. FLAG CONTRADICTION NOTED, NOT WRITTEN: Aurora's R carries a hardCC flag in the kit file, but Riot's own description says only that the shockwave 'damages and slows'. Per the brief's rule I trusted the description and never described the R as hard CC anywhere. Someone should check whether that flag is a tooltip-parsing misfire, because it will be affecting other Aurora matchups too.
